g.text: How often would crashes have to happen to wipe out the premium?

g.text: Data: Cboe via FRED (VIXCLS); S&P 500 via Yahoo Finance. Sign: implied − realised (positive = variance seller gains). Break-even: a share g / (g − L) of months would have to be crashes of

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: the mean size L for the mean payoff to be zero (g = mean of the other months; 95% CI from the block bootstrap). Observed: crashes seen in the sample, exact Poisson 95% CI. A blue point

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: below the whole orange bar = the premium covers crashes of that size even if they are as frequent as the data allow.
